# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Short answer:** Panasonic Eneloop Pro is the best all-rounder, and IKEA LADDA is the best value if you can get to an IKEA.

## My picks

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA.** Digital Camera World's reviewer has used them for years in flash testing and reports 100% reliability. Specs are 2600 mAh, about 85% charge kept after 1 year, and roughly 500 recharges. The downsides are a higher price and fewer cycles than the standard version. [Retailer links are in the Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) (Amazon, Adorama, Newegg, Best Buy). It lists prices from about $22 to $35, but I can't confirm the pack size.

**Best for longevity and low-drain devices: standard Panasonic Eneloop AA.** It holds 2000 mAh, is rated for 2,100 recharges, and keeps 70% of its charge after 10 years. It suits remotes, clocks, and devices you rarely recharge. [Buy links are in the same guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries).

**Best value: IKEA LADDA.** Charge-Test's capacity tests found the LADDA 2450 mAh cells close to Eneloop Pro and the 1900 mAh cells close to standard Eneloop. They think IKEA's supplier is Panasonic, though IKEA has never confirmed this ([Charge-Test](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)). IKEA's US site currently lists the [LADDA AA 1900 mAh 4-pack for $9.99](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/). Prices of $7.99 in other sources are in euros or unverified for the US. I didn't see the 2450 mAh version on the US page, so check your local store.

**Best in bulk: Tenergy Premium PRO 2800 mAh.** It's a 20-pack for $42.99 (about $2.15 per cell), with a 4-pack at $11.99. The maker claims 85% charge kept after 1 year and 1,200 cycles. Those are manufacturer figures that I didn't see independently tested, and the warranty terms conflict (12 months vs. 90 days). [Buy at Tenergy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack). This is an affiliate link, and the page notes they earn a commission.

**For voltage-sensitive devices: EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA.** These output 1.5V like alkalines instead of the 1.2V of NiMH cells, which helps devices that read 1.2V as "low." [See the Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) for links.

## Caveats
- **Amazon Basics High-Capacity** gets conflicting reviews. [GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/) recommends it only for low-drain devices, while the Frame & Focal tests ([one](https://frameandfocal.com/camera-reviews/which-aa-rechargeable-battery-gives-you-the-best-bang-for-your-buck), [two](https://frameandfocal.com/camera-reviews/which-aa-rechargeable-battery-best-after-one-year-abuse-440920)) found it weak under load. Those two articles also contradict each other on some numbers, so I'd treat their figures cautiously. I'd skip it for cameras, flashes, or flashlights.
- **Chargers:** Use a decent smart charger, since mismatched or cheap chargers shorten battery life.
- **Voltage:** NiMH cells are 1.2V nominal, so a few devices built strictly for 1.5V alkalines may show a low-battery warning.

Tell me what devices you'll use them in and I can narrow it to one pick.
